To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we identified a multicity outbreak caused by a linezolid-resistant, cfr-containing S. epidermidis strain that was identical at the genomic level in two hospitals; 2) the cfr-containing clone had been circulating in hospital A for at least two years prior to the outbreak, and 3) the cfr gene was located on the plasmid pLZ1.
we report a multicity cfr-containing line zolid-resistant Staph. epidermidis outbreak in Ohio.

the identification and characterization of a new type of cfr-containing, linezolid-resistant S. epidermidis strain.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
linezolid-resistant S. epidermidis is an emerging problem in healthcare settings.
a linezolid-resistant strain of S. epidermidis with the cfr gene was transmitted between 2 hospitals in Ohio.
the outbreak was caused by the clonal spread of cfr-containing S. epidermidis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cfr gene was present in the majority of linezolid- resistant isolates, but the cfr-containing clone was the only clone to spread from hospital A to B.
the cfr gene is a major contributor to resistance to the oxazolidinone antibiotic linezolid in Staphylococci.
the cfr-containing clone is spreading in the community and causing outbreaks in hospitals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cfr-containing line-zolid-resistant S. epidermidis is circulating in the community and is capable of clonal spread in hospitals.
linezolid resistance in staphylococci is not always due to a ribosomal mutation, and the cfr gene may be a potential source of resistance in the hospital setting.
the cfr-containing clone is widespread, and it is likely to continue to be a problem.
